body:
Part of #102, under #100 toward #36. Depends on the completed first-transfer/frozen-handoff child linked below.

## Outcome

Measure the incremental cost of porting one further extant Agda proof into the working Lean fragment, and decide whether selective porting merits further investment. This is an experiment with an admissible negative or inconclusive outcome, not a requirement to manufacture a successful second port.

## Mandatory role separation and test protocol

- A distinct proof author must conduct the test in a fresh session. The author must not have implemented or reviewed the framework or first port, and must not inherit those agents' conversation, scratch work, private notes or solution plans. A fresh session of the same implementer does not satisfy this requirement. For agent delegation, use a new agent with `fork_turns="none"` (or the platform's equivalent), supplying only this task and the frozen public handoff. The orchestrator must not execute this child itself after implementing the preceding children.
- Record the author/session provenance and frozen commit. Ordinary repository source, public documentation, the first-port example, pinned upstream Agda source and standard public references are allowed inputs. Declare the actual inputs. This tests documented reuse rather than blind theorem proving.
- The independent author selects one further extant theorem whose declaration-level dependencies fit the frozen supported fragment. Before attempting its Lean proof, record the exact upstream revision/license/declaration, dependency closure, intended source conclusion, expected semantic applications and a prospective stopping rule/effort budget. Do not choose a reflexive restatement or renamed copy of tr-concat. Obtain an independent scope check without supplying a proof solution. If no suitable theorem can be identified, report that finding rather than silently adding language rules.
- Freeze the candidate and protocol before proof construction. Framework/first-port implementers must not pre-port it, supply theorem-specific helpers or skeletons, or coach the baseline attempt. Generic helpers already in the frozen interface are allowed. Record any accidental contamination; a contaminated attempt cannot satisfy the independent baseline gate and must be rerun with an unexposed author and, if the solution leaked, another scoped theorem.
- During the baseline attempt the interface is read-only. The author may write proof-local helpers and record them as incremental effort. Missing API, unsupported rules, failures, questions and workarounds are outcomes, not reasons for hidden implementer intervention. Do not improve the frozen interface midway and call the result the baseline.
- Save the attempt and report before feedback to the implementers. Afterward, interface improvements and an assisted retry may be useful, but must be reported separately and cannot replace the original independent result. A claim that improvements reduce fresh-author effort requires another uncontaminated test; do not start an unbounded sequence of ports automatically.

## Evidence and decision

- Record Agda-to-Lean declaration/proof-step correspondence and whether the argument was preserved.
- Separate framework construction from incremental proof translation, dependency discovery, helper writing and debugging. Report actual available effort measurements, command failures, author interventions and API changes without fabricated time estimates.
- Identify what was reused unchanged, what plumbing reached the author, and which proposed helpers could serve other proofs.
- For a successful transfer, retain the source derivation and applications through existing soundness, with EDD/statement review, fresh build and exhaustive audit. An ordinary semantic proof alone does not establish transfer. Keep failed scratch work outside the production import closure and archive enough evidence to explain an unsuccessful attempt.
- Compare the route with a direct Lean proof of the selected result: what extra cost buys reuse across models, and whether that benefit is demonstrated or remains prospective. State limitations of one small follow-up experiment; do not extrapolate to a whole library.
- An evaluator distinct from the framework/first-port implementers reviews the evidence and recommends: continue bounded selective porting; improve the interface and retest; or reconsider the route (for example direct Lean developments using Agda as a mathematical reference, or narrower domain-specific proof interfaces).
- Publish the report and recommendation on #102/#100 and feed it into #103's entry gate. Negative evidence is acceptable completion of this experiment, but cannot waive #102's original technical acceptance or authorize an alternative implementation automatically.

## Completion gate

This child cannot close on a second proof written by the first implementer, on an assisted attempt reported as independent, or on a narrative usability claim without the recorded attempt. The fresh-author baseline and independent evaluation are mandatory even if the first port looks easy. The approved scope is one further proof and its assessment; broader ports require a later decision.

Blocked by: #105.

comments.body:
Tracker reconciliation, 2026-10-25: closing the completed scoped delivery. The independent author experiment and its evaluation were accepted as a completed negative experiment. The general associativity transfer was unfinished at the prospective budget. The archived evidence and separate evaluator recommend interface repair and retest; this is not a successful second proof port.

I inspected the retained independent-review/originator records and verified that commit `429c7cc` has exactly the same Git tree as accepted snapshot `ad14b6740d7553e34083672396b4a8b4595da46b`. This reconciles an omitted issue-state transition; it does not claim a new implementation review or fresh current-HEAD build. The public parent report records the acceptance: https://github.com/VladimirMarko/conaled/issues/102#issuecomment-6322541685.

#102 stays open for #107's incomplete repair and #108's independent retest. #103's smooth entry gate remains intact. Historical baseline evidence is unchanged.

title: Evaluate Agda proof reuse with an independent fresh author
